sources_considered.why: Reports that the planned October 2024 generative-AI Alexa launch did not happen.
Counterevidence: Gemini Live, an LLM replacement for Google Assistant, rolled out in 2024.

receipt.public_excerpt: Amazon had been planning to roll out a new Alexa powered by generative AI in October 2024, but that obviously didn't happen.

evidence_items.explanation: The LLM-powered Alexa was not released in 2024. So LLMs did not improve the named assistant that year.

receipt.public_excerpt: Hallucinations have to be "close to zero," Rohit Prasad, leader of Amazon's artificial general intelligence (AGI) team told FT.

evidence_items.explanation: Amazon's AI lead cited hallucinations as a reason for the delay, which is consistent with the claim's reasoning.

receipt.public_excerpt: Gemini Live is billed as a “mobile conversational experience” and is the AI-powered replacement for Google Assistant.

evidence_items.explanation: Google shipped an LLM-based replacement for Google Assistant to Android users in 2024. This is the strongest counterpoint, but the source does not show it was markedly better at assistant tasks.

unresolved_gaps: No source assessed whether Gemini Live or Apple's December 2024 ChatGPT handoff in Siri markedly improved those assistants.
Amazon's own statement on the 2024 delay was not read directly.
